newsitem.title: UK: Group sees rising risk of double hull tanker crack.
newsitem.headline: Group sees rising risk of double hull tanker crack.

text.p: The Salvage Association warned on Friday that its surveys had uncovered an increasing incidence of cracking in relatively new double hull tankers.

Although the association said the number of major structural failures to tankers and bulk carriers was reducing, its principal naval architect John Waite pointed to a growing problem with double hull vessels.
"During damage surveys on a number of vessels extensive fatigue cracking was found to be compromising the strength and integrity of the double bottom ballast tank structure," he said.

Corrosion was not considered to be significant in most cases, but specialist and high tensile strength steels had been used in the ships' construction, Waite said. Some vessels had been under eight years old.
Waite said that although the problems had not been life threatening they had involved underwriters in claims for repairs in excess of $1 million per vessel.
The defects demonstrated the need for vigilance to ensure cracks were discovered before they became structurally catastrophic, he said.
Damage was discovered in two cases when crews noted changes in the soundings of ballast tanks while at sea, he said.
-- Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
